q: A linter checks your code by …
why: That is static analysis: checking code by looking at it, not executing it.

q: Which finding is most likely a real bug?
o: An undefined name such as dat
why: Using a name that doesn't exist crashes when that line runs; the others are style or smells.

q: Which tool only makes the layout consistent and doesn't look for bugs?
why: A formatter such as Black or Prettier rewrites spacing and line breaks only.

q: Which check can tell you load() returns the wrong user?
why: Only tests run the code with real inputs and compare the output.

q: node --check finds a typo in a variable name inside a function.
why: Myth: it only checks that the file parses, so the typo fails later in the browser.

q: A linter can warn about code that is actually fine.
why: Fact: that is a false positive, which is why linters have ignore comments.
